title: Protest Decisions in the Employer's Favour — Employer Benefit Charging Adjudicator Reference
content:
## Rule

Under Employer Benefit Charging, when a pending protest of benefit charges is granted, the position is relieved and a relief credit is posted for the protest decision.

The relief credit of a protest decision is fixed only after the position carries a pending written protest of the statement, with the protest ground and the protest date recorded on it.

Put the other way round: while the position shows no pending written protest of the statement with its protest ground and protest date recorded, no relief credit of a protest decision is fixed.

## Capability

`grant_charge_protest_0f56e95e` decides a pending protest of benefit charges in the employer's favour and books the relief credit it carries. One call moves the employer's chargeable position from protest pending to relieved with the relief basis given, and posts one credit with credit reason `relief_granted`, dated today and counted in today's calendar quarter, against the single posted benefit charge named, for the dollar amount given; the position's total charged falls by that amount. The employer sees the position as relieved and the credit on its next statement or reimbursement bill.

## How it is invoked

An agent-side tool: the agent unlocks `grant_charge_protest_0f56e95e` and then calls it.

## Parameters

- `charge_position_id` — Id. The reference number of the chargeable position whose pending protest is decided, as returned by the charge position lookup.
- `customer_id` — Id. The employer's customer reference number that owns the position, as returned by the customer profile lookup.
- `source_charge_id` — Id. The reference number of the posted benefit charge the relief credit reduces, as returned by the charge ledger lookup.
- `relief_basis` — Enum. The ground on which relief is granted:
  - `none` — no relief; not used for a granted protest
  - `voluntary_quit_without_good_cause` — the claimant left this employer voluntarily without good cause attributable to it
  - `discharge_misconduct` — this employer discharged the claimant for misconduct connected with the work
  - `refused_suitable_work` — the claimant refused suitable work this employer offered
  - `continuing_part_time` — this employer still employs the claimant part time as in the base period
  - `agency_error` — the benefits were paid in error by the agency
  - `not_base_period_employer` — this employer paid no base-period wages or the wages charged to it are wrong
  - `appeal_decision` — an appeal decision relieved the employer; not used for a protest
- `relief_credit_amount` — US dollars, rounded to 2 decimal places, a plain positive number without a currency sign. The dollar amount of the relief credit booked against the named charge.

## Return

A receipt with `credit_reference` (reference number of the relief credit just posted), `charge_position_id` (the position decided), `source_charge_id` (the posted charge credited), `relief_basis` (the basis recorded), `relief_credit_amount` (dollars credited, 2 decimal places), `credit_quarter` (YYYY-Qn, the calendar quarter in which the credit is posted), `total_charged_after` (the position's total charged once the credit is booked, 2 decimal places) and `position_status` (always `relieved` once decided). A receipt carrying a `credit_reference` means the protest was granted and the credit posted.

## Contract notes

- The credit is dated the day of the call and counted in that day's calendar quarter, whatever quarter the protested statement covers.
- One call books one credit against one named posted charge.
